correctness.rationale: Discrete Fourier orthogonality at n+1 angular points diagonalizes the polynomial sampling Gram with eigenvalues lambda_k=e^-t1 t1^k/k!+e^-t2 t2^k/k!. Uniform Stirling for t_j=n*a_j with positive a_j produces I(s|a)=a-s+s log(s/a). For R<1/e, convex sublevel intervals of I cover s=0 and s=1 only if the first radius a<=R and the second meets I(1|b)<=R. Among such centers, a=R maximizes first right reach eR; b=b_R the smaller root of I(1|b)=R minimizes the second left endpoint. Strict contact of these endpoints uniquely requires rho=b/R>e solving rho-1=e log rho and (rho-1)R-1-log(rho R)=0, giving rho≈5.7591317338, R*=0.1055733636919 and second center rho*R≈0.6080109091. Every R<R* leaves an uncovered gap, and at R* the whole [0,1] is covered. Uniform factorial errors and compactified subsequences of arbitrary radii yield -log B_n/n ->R* and asymptotically unique normalized radii. Independently numerically solved both contact equations and a dense s-grid matched R*; this finite computation does not replace global convexity/compactness proof.
residual_risks: Numerical covering only samples points; global optimizer and arbitrary changing radii require the analytic endpoint and compactness steps.
